rule_authority.gap: No baseline mechanic registry entry or approved field-authority matrix exists for a card semantic projection/compiler or a new semantic taxonomy.
rule_authority.required_resolution: Approve one migration-only mechanic record and map every semantic operation to an active rule clause, existing machine/effect fields, established owner, privacy, and persistence=none.

findings.title: Semantic field rule authority is not established
findings.risk: Production fields or policy could be invented from code, tests, text, or historical behavior without active product authority.
findings.required_gate: Approve one migration-only mechanic record and a per-field authority/owner/privacy/persistence matrix; fail closed on unmapped meaning.

findings.title: Canonical semantic source and deletion path are missing
findings.risk: A sidecar or duplicate AI/Presentation mapping would become a third long-term card authority and drift from both catalog generations.
findings.required_gate: Select one canonical v0.6 authored location, one typed read path, and an explicit deletion gate for any read-only legacy adapter.

findings.title: Arbitrary card-id lookup can expose hidden candidates
findings.risk: AI could enrich future supply-bag or obscured belt identities even if returned semantic keys themselves are public-safe.
findings.required_gate: AI accepts semantics only for a revision-bound definition/provenance envelope from an existing own-hand or public-rack visibility port; expose no enumeration or arbitrary-ID API.

findings.title: AI scores and policy weights must be excluded from public definitions
findings.risk: Public/catalog utility values would create a second AI policy owner and leak hidden reasoning through presentation or diagnostics.
findings.required_gate: Recursively reject AI score, utility, policy-weight, reason, candidate, plan, learning, and policy fields; the rule-authorized region_supply_weight remains a supply field rather than AI utility; AI applies all private weights after the neutral typed read.

findings.title: Semantic projection must not become a second card engine
findings.risk: Legality, execution, queue, target, or effect ownership could be duplicated behind a generic semantic service.
findings.required_gate: Semantic code is read-only and has zero imports from queue/execution/effect owners in either direction.

findings.title: Localized-text inference and specific-card branching are forbidden
findings.risk: Text/name matching creates language-dependent hidden rules and one-off card behavior that diverges from machine fields.
findings.required_gate: Compile only closed active effect kinds and validated machine fields; reject card-id/name/family/localized-text branches.

findings.title: Presentation must remain the sole UI-rule owner
findings.risk: Semantic data could encode copy, icons, chips, layout, tooltips, animation, or action state and become a competing presentation engine.
findings.required_gate: Semantic output is neutral mechanics only; CardPresentationRuntimeService owns every card-facing presentation decision.

findings.title: Compilation must occur once per stable definition fingerprint
findings.risk: Per-target, per-score, per-frame, or per-comparison compilation would multiply candidate cost and blur compiler versus AI ownership.
findings.required_gate: Cache by semantic schema, catalog identity, and definition fingerprint; repeated AI and Presentation reads are cache hits and return detached copies.

findings.title: Semantic data adds no persistence or randomness
findings.risk: A saved cache, new section, random fallback, or tie-break would alter deterministic continuation and owner count.
findings.required_gate: Save remains exactly 19 sections; semantic cache is rebuilt; compile/query leaves RunRngService checkpoint unchanged.

findings.title: Integration must be typed, scene-owned, and Main-free
findings.risk: A Main callback, dynamic method-name route, service locator, or script-only runtime helper would violate the extinction and scene acceptance policies.
findings.required_gate: Typed injection under GameRuntimeCoordinator, editable production scene plus Bench/MCP evidence for new runtime responsibility, and negative Main dependency scans.

findings.title: Retired and unavailable mechanics must fail closed
findings.risk: Compilation could make retired or catalog-present-but-unavailable content visible, scoreable, purchasable, or executable.
findings.required_gate: Reject retired identifiers and keep deferred organization content out of active acquisition, AI candidates, and player surfaces.

findings.title: Snapshot needs closed schema identity and provenance
findings.risk: Unversioned or mutable dictionaries make drift, stale cache, and non-data leakage difficult to detect.
findings.required_gate: Version/fingerprint the snapshot, reject unknown/nonfinite/Object values, and return detached pure data.

findings.title: Shared hot files require one integration writer
findings.risk: Parallel schema, AI, Presentation, and integration branches can collide in catalogs and coordinator composition.
findings.required_gate: Merge schema first, then typed consumers, then one integration-writer composition change.

findings.title: Diagnostics must expose counters rather than private payloads
findings.risk: Debug snapshots could leak scores, candidate lists, owner truth, hands, targets, or future bag order.
findings.required_gate: Allow only schema/fingerprint/readiness/cache counters and public-safe validation codes.

findings.title: Existing queue and execution ownership can remain untouched
findings.conclusion: A read-only semantic projection can remain outside the execution graph.

findings.title: Save and RNG authorities are unambiguous
findings.conclusion: No semantic persistence or randomness is required.

findings.title: Current v0.6 catalog structured scan has zero retired-identifier hits
findings.conclusion: All 348 current v0.6 records scanned clean for retired contract identifiers and legacy panic/heat keys; a permanent validator is still required.

findings.title: Existing scene seams support typed semantic consumers
findings.conclusion: A narrow query port can be injected without a Main dependency or second process loop.

hard_invariants.name: no_second_card_state_owner_or_engine
hard_invariants.gate: Semantic code owns no card instance, hand, queue, timing, target, legality, execution, effect, cooldown, history, or settlement state.

hard_invariants.name: no_ai_score_in_public_definitions
hard_invariants.gate: No AI score, utility, policy-weight, priority, reason, candidate, plan, learning, or policy coefficient is stored in public/catalog semantic output.

hard_invariants.name: no_localized_text_rules
hard_invariants.gate: Machine semantics never parse or match display/rules text, localization keys, tooltips, or translated keywords.

hard_invariants.name: no_ui_rules
hard_invariants.gate: Semantic data owns no color, icon, chip order, copy, layout, tooltip, animation, or action-state decision.

hard_invariants.name: no_save_section
hard_invariants.gate: No new save key, owner binding, restore hook, or twentieth v0.6 section; cache is rebuilt.

hard_invariants.name: no_rng_change
hard_invariants.gate: Zero draws, streams, seeds, shuffles, random fallbacks, or tie-break changes; checkpoint equality is tested.

hard_invariants.name: no_retired_mechanics
hard_invariants.gate: Retired identifiers fail validation and cannot enter candidates, presentation, execution, AI, or persistence.

hard_invariants.name: no_untyped_or_main_bypass
hard_invariants.gate: No Main/current-scene lookup, dynamic call/get/set/has_method, string callback, or compatibility fallback.

hard_invariants.name: no_candidate_hidden_information
hard_invariants.gate: AI receives semantics only after own-hand/public-rack/belt visibility authorization; no arbitrary ID lookup or enumeration exists on the AI port.

hard_invariants.name: no_per_score_compilation
hard_invariants.gate: At most one compile per stable definition fingerprint and semantic schema version; scoring is cache-read only.

hard_invariants.name: no_specific_card_branching
hard_invariants.gate: No card-id, card-name, family-name, or localized-tag code branch; use closed active effect kinds and authored fields.

hard_invariants.name: no_dual_long_term_authority
hard_invariants.gate: One canonical authored semantic source and one typed read path; temporary legacy adapters have a named deletion gate and are never writable authorities.

hard_invariants.name: fail_closed_on_unknown_meaning
hard_invariants.gate: Any untraceable field is RULE_AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED, not a generic inferred behavior.

recommended_safe_boundary.canonical_data: Neutral rule-backed semantic descriptors live with the eventual authoritative v0.6 machine definition or typed Resource representation; no runtime sidecar is created.

Legacy adapter scope and physical deletion gate documented.

No specific-card/name/family/localized-text branch.
AI reads bind typed own-hand/public-rack or viewer-legal belt provenance and source revision.
AI API has no arbitrary-ID lookup, enumeration, future-bag, or obscured-card path.
Scores, weights, reasons, candidates, plans, and learning remain private in AiRuntimeController.
Play, buy, counter, and supply candidate set/order/score/selection plus RNG parity pass.

Public, owner-private, rival-private, obscured-belt, and final-audit recursive leak tests pass.

No Main/current-scene/dynamic method-name dependency or fallback; negative scans pass.

Compile count is at most one per definition fingerprint/schema; repeated reads are cache hits.

Focused headless tests cover positive/negative schema, privacy, authority, parity, and cache cases.
Editable production scene and production-wiring Bench exist for any new runtime responsibility.
